_about: Derived from the ProbeMatrix 9M framework (Eyekyam). Action catalogues remain in the ProbeMatrix CAPA Zone.

chapters.title: Manpower/Mindpower
chapters.definition: Whether the people doing the work were ready for it, and what the organisation did to make them ready.

subcategories.name: Selection and Qualification
subcategories.definition: How people were chosen and placed in a role, and whether their qualifications matched what the job really needed.
probes: Did the people in the role hold the qualifications the task called for?
Was the job's real demand written down before people were chosen for it?
Were gaps found at selection followed up before the person worked alone?

subcategories.name: Training Programme Design and Delivery
subcategories.definition: Whether training was built around the real task and delivered so that people could use it on the job.
probes: Was the training built from the task as it is really done?
Did the training cover the abnormal and rare conditions met in this event?
Could people practise the skill before they needed it for real?

subcategories.name: Competence Assessment and Authorisation
subcategories.definition: How the organisation confirmed that someone could do the work safely before letting them do it.
probes: Was competence checked by watching the work, not only by a course record?
Did someone with the right standing sign the authorisation for this task?
Were authorisations reviewed when the task or the equipment changed?

subcategories.name: Workload Management
subcategories.definition: Whether the amount and mix of work given to people left them enough time and attention to do it safely.
probes: Was the number of people on shift right for the work planned that day?
Did anyone have more tasks running at once than they could track?
Was there a way to say the load was too high and have it acted on?

subcategories.name: Fatigue Risk Management
subcategories.definition: How rosters, shift length and rest were set and watched so that tiredness did not erode performance.
probes: Were shift lengths and rest breaks inside the site's own limits?
Did the event happen in a part of the shift known for low alertness?
Was tiredness something people could report without a cost to them?

subcategories.name: Cognitive Readiness and Situational Awareness
subcategories.definition: Whether people had the information and mental picture they needed to notice, understand and anticipate the hazard.
probes: Did people have a clear picture of the plant state before acting?
Were the cues that something was wrong visible to them in time?
Was the picture shared across the people who needed it?

subcategories.name: Psychological Readiness and Support
subcategories.definition: Whether people were in a fit state of mind for the work, and what support existed when they were not.
probes: Were known stressors on the team recognised before the work began?
Was support available to people after earlier difficult events?
Could someone step back from a task without being judged for it?

subcategories.name: Communication and Coordination
subcategories.definition: How information passed between people and teams, including handovers, briefings and messages during the work.
probes: Did the handover pass on every live hazard and open job?
Were messages confirmed back so both sides knew they matched?
Did teams working on the same system know what the others were doing?

subcategories.name: Team Dynamics
subcategories.definition: How the team worked together: shared goals, trust, roles and the way disagreements were handled.
probes: Were roles in the team clear to everyone on the job?
Did team members check each other's work as a normal habit?
Was a doubt raised by one member taken up by the rest?

subcategories.name: Leadership and Authority Gradient
subcategories.definition: How rank and seniority shaped who spoke up, who decided and whether challenges reached the decision maker.
probes: Could a junior person stop the job if they saw a problem?
Did leaders ask for views before deciding on the risky step?
Were challenges from the floor recorded and answered?

subcategories.name: Cultural and Organisational Climate
subcategories.definition: The shared beliefs and habits around the work that made some choices feel normal and others feel hard.
probes: Was reporting a concern treated as useful rather than as trouble?
Had a shortcut become the usual way of working without anyone deciding it?
Did what leaders rewarded match what the rules asked for?

subcategories.name: Error Propensity and Human Limitations
subcategories.definition: The known limits of human attention, memory and perception, and whether the work was designed around them.
probes: Did the task depend on someone remembering a step with no prompt?
Were similar-looking items or readings easy to confuse?
Had the design allowed for the slips that people predictably make?

subcategories.name: Competence Sustainability and Continuous Improvement
subcategories.definition: How skills were kept fresh over time, especially for rare tasks, and how lessons were fed back into training.
probes: Were rarely used skills refreshed before they were needed?
Did lessons from earlier events reach the training content?
Was there a record of when each person last did this task?

chapters.title: Medium
chapters.definition: The physical and psychological surroundings of the work, and how they made it easier or harder to do safely.

subcategories.name: Physical Environment Controls
subcategories.definition: How temperature, ventilation, lighting and similar conditions at the workplace were kept within safe limits.
probes: Were conditions at the work location measured or checked before the job?
Did the conditions on the day fall outside what the plan assumed?
Was there a control in place for the condition that mattered here?

subcategories.name: Workspace Ergonomics and Human Fit
subcategories.definition: Whether the layout, reach, posture and access at the workplace fitted the people and the task.
probes: Could people reach and see what they needed without strain?
Did the layout force awkward or unsafe positions during the task?
Were the users asked about the layout when it was designed?

subcategories.name: Noise and Auditory Environment
subcategories.definition: How noise and sound affected hearing alarms, speech and other cues the work relied on.
probes: Could alarms and voices be heard clearly at the work location?
Did hearing protection or background noise mask an important cue?
Was the sound environment considered when alarms were chosen?

subcategories.name: Visual Environment and Legibility
subcategories.definition: Whether people could see the work, the plant and its labels and displays clearly enough to read them right.
probes: Was the lighting enough to read labels and gauges at the time?
Were tags, signs and displays legible from where people stood?
Did glare, smoke or darkness hide something people needed to see?

subcategories.name: Localised Hazards and Exposure
subcategories.definition: Hazards specific to a spot in the plant, such as releases, hot surfaces or toxic gas, and how exposure was limited.
probes: Was the local hazard at this spot known and marked?
Were people kept out of the exposure zone while it was live?
Did monitoring cover the place where the release happened?

subcategories.name: Operational Environment and Tempo
subcategories.definition: The pace and state of operations around the work, such as start-ups, upsets or many jobs running at once.
probes: Was the work done during an unusual plant state or transition?
Were several jobs running at once in the same area?
Did the pace of operations leave time to pause and check?

subcategories.name: Psychological Environment and Stressors
subcategories.definition: Pressures in the work setting, such as time pressure, conflict or uncertainty, that weighed on people's choices.
probes: Was there pressure to finish the job within a fixed window?
Did conflicting instructions leave people unsure what to do?
Were stressful conditions known to supervision before the event?

subcategories.name: Cultural Environment and Norms
subcategories.definition: The unwritten local norms of the work area that shaped how tasks were really done.
probes: Did the local way of working differ from the written method?
Was the local norm known to supervisors and left as it was?
Would a newcomer have picked up the shortcut from colleagues?

subcategories.name: Environmental Stressors and Extreme Conditions
subcategories.definition: Weather, heat, cold, rain, wind or night conditions that made the work or the response harder.
probes: Did the weather or time of day affect the work or the response?
Were extreme conditions planned for in the method or the emergency plan?
Was there a trigger to stop work when conditions got worse?

subcategories.name: External Environment and Stakeholders
subcategories.definition: Neighbours, regulators, contractors and other outside parties whose presence or demands shaped the risk.
probes: Did people or assets outside the fence sit within the hazard zone?
Were outside parties told what they needed to know in time?
Did an outside demand change how or when the work was done?

subcategories.name: Infrastructure, Access, and Traffic Interfaces
subcategories.definition: Roads, routes, access points and shared corridors, and how they affected the work and the emergency response.
probes: Could responders reach the scene by a clear route?
Did pipelines, roads or vehicles share space in a way that added risk?
Were access restrictions in place and kept to during the work?

subcategories.name: Emergency Preparedness in Environmental Contexts
subcategories.definition: Whether emergency arrangements fitted the actual setting, including layout, weather and neighbouring sites.
probes: Did the emergency plan match the real layout of the area?
Were detection and alarm coverage right for this location?
Had drills tested the plan in conditions like those on the day?

chapters.title: Method
chapters.definition: The procedures, processes and ways of working used to plan, carry out and control the task.

subcategories.name: Procedure Design and Development
subcategories.definition: How procedures were written, by whom, and whether they were tested against the task as it is really done.
probes: Was the procedure written with the people who do the task?
Was it tried out on the job before it was issued?
Did it cover the conditions met during this event?

subcategories.name: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
subcategories.definition: Whether an approved written method existed for the task, was current and was available at the point of use.
probes: Did an approved SOP exist for this task?
Was the version in use the current one?
Could people get to it where and when they did the work?

subcategories.name: Compliance and Adherence
subcategories.definition: How far work followed the written method, and why the gaps between the two existed.
probes: Was the written method followed on the day?
Where it was not, did the method fit the work as done?
Were earlier departures from the method noticed and discussed?

subcategories.name: Flexibility and Adaptability
subcategories.definition: Whether the method allowed safe adjustment when conditions changed, and who could decide on a change.
probes: Did the method say what to do when conditions changed?
Was it clear who could approve a change on the spot?
Were on-the-spot changes reviewed afterwards?

subcategories.name: Documentation and Communication
subcategories.definition: How methods, permits and records were written down, shared and kept so that the next person could rely on them.
probes: Were permits and job records complete for this work?
Did the records travel with the job between shifts?
Could a later reader tell what was done and why?

subcategories.name: Risk Management Integration
subcategories.definition: Whether hazard identification and risk assessment were built into the method rather than done apart from it.
probes: Was a task risk assessment done for this job?
Did its controls appear as steps in the method?
Was the assessment revisited when the job changed?

subcategories.name: Alignment with Technology
subcategories.definition: Whether the method matched the equipment, software and controls actually installed.
probes: Did the method describe the equipment as it was installed?
Were changes to the equipment carried into the method?
Did the control system support the steps the method asked for?

subcategories.name: Emergency and Contingency Procedures
subcategories.definition: The written arrangements for upsets and emergencies, and whether they worked when used.
probes: Was there a written response for this kind of release or upset?
Did the response steps work in the time available?
Were the people on duty familiar with those steps?

subcategories.name: Continuous Improvement
subcategories.definition: How methods were reviewed and changed using findings from audits, near misses and earlier events.
probes: Were earlier findings about this method acted on?
Was there a set review date for the method, and was it kept?
Did users have a way to propose changes to it?

subcategories.name: Simplicity and Accessibility
subcategories.definition: Whether the method was short, clear and easy enough to use under real working conditions.
probes: Could the method be followed without needing outside help?
Were the key steps easy to find in the document?
Was the language plain for the people who used it?

chapters.title: Mission
chapters.definition: The goals, priorities and targets the organisation set, and the pressure they put on decisions about risk.

subcategories.name: Strategic Objectives and Priorities
subcategories.definition: How the organisation's top-level aims ranked safety against output, cost and schedule.
probes: Did stated priorities put safety ahead of output in practice?
Were trade-offs between goals made openly and recorded?
Did senior decisions in this case follow the stated priorities?

subcategories.name: Operational Goals and Targets
subcategories.definition: The day-to-day targets set for the site or team, and whether they pushed people towards risk.
probes: Did a production or schedule target bear on this work?
Were targets ever relaxed when safety needed more time?
Did people feel judged on targets more than on safe work?

subcategories.name: Resource Allocation
subcategories.definition: How people, time and equipment were shared out across goals, and whether safety-critical work got its share.
probes: Did this work get the people and time it needed?
Was safety-critical work deferred to free resources for other goals?
Was there a way to ask for more resources and get an answer?

subcategories.name: Leadership and Accountability
subcategories.definition: Who owned each goal and decision, and whether that ownership was clear, accepted and followed through.
probes: Was it clear who owned the decision that mattered here?
Did that owner have the authority and the information to act?
Were open decisions tracked until someone closed them?

subcategories.name: Risk Tolerance and Decision-Making
subcategories.definition: How much risk the organisation was willing to accept, and how decisions near that limit were made.
probes: Was there a stated limit on the risk the site would accept?
Were decisions near that limit escalated to the right level?
Did known risks stay open for a long time without a decision?

subcategories.name: External Influences and Stakeholder Expectations
subcategories.definition: Pressures from customers, owners, regulators or the public that shaped goals and choices.
probes: Did an outside commitment shape the timing of this work?
Were regulator or partner expectations met on paper only?
Did outside pressure change what was reported upwards?

subcategories.name: Mission Complexity and Clarity
subcategories.definition: Whether the task and its purpose were clear, and whether its complexity was recognised and planned for.
probes: Was the purpose of the task clear to everyone doing it?
Was the task's complexity recognised when it was planned?
Did the plan say what success and stopping points looked like?

subcategories.name: Organisational Culture and Mission Alignment
subcategories.definition: Whether the organisation's culture supported its stated goals or quietly worked against them.
probes: Did daily habits match what the organisation said it valued?
Was raising a safety issue seen as part of the job?
Were known gaps between values and habits ever discussed?

subcategories.name: Communication and Mission Integration
subcategories.definition: How goals and priorities were explained down the line so that each level understood its part.
probes: Were the site's priorities explained to the people doing the work?
Did each level know how its tasks fed the wider goals?
Were changes in priority passed on promptly?

subcategories.name: Continuous Evaluation and Improvement
subcategories.definition: How the organisation checked whether its goals and targets were still right, and changed them when they were not.
probes: Were goals reviewed after earlier events or audits?
Did reviews look at the side effects of targets on safety?
Was there evidence that a goal was changed because of a lesson?

chapters.title: Measurement
chapters.definition: How the organisation measured, monitored and analysed performance and safety, and acted on what it found.

subcategories.name: Metrics Design and Relevance
subcategories.definition: Whether the measures in use tracked the hazards that mattered, not only the easy-to-count outcomes.
probes: Did any measure track the hazard behind this event?
Were the measures chosen for their link to major risk?
Would the measures have shown the problem growing?

subcategories.name: Data Collection and Accuracy
subcategories.definition: How data was gathered and checked, and whether it could be trusted.
probes: Was the data on this system collected as planned?
Were readings and records checked for errors?
Did gaps in the data go unnoticed?

subcategories.name: Monitoring and Reporting Systems
subcategories.definition: The systems that watched plant and work in real time or by routine reports, and whether they flagged problems.
probes: Did monitoring cover the equipment and area involved?
Were alarms or reports raised before the event?
Did anyone act on what the monitoring showed?

subcategories.name: Analysis and Interpretation
subcategories.definition: How data was turned into understanding, and whether trends and weak signals were spotted.
probes: Was the data on this problem ever analysed for trends?
Were repeated small failures linked together?
Did the analysis reach someone able to act on it?

subcategories.name: Feedback Loops
subcategories.definition: How results of measurement went back to the people and processes that could change things.
probes: Did findings from monitoring reach the people doing the work?
Were actions from earlier findings checked for effect?
Did the loop close, or did findings stop at a report?

subcategories.name: Benchmarking and Comparisons
subcategories.definition: Whether performance was compared with other sites, peers or good practice, and gaps acted on.
probes: Was this site's performance compared with similar sites?
Were lessons from other sites' events looked at here?
Did comparison lead to any change before this event?

subcategories.name: Predictive Analytics and Risk Indicators
subcategories.definition: Forward-looking measures meant to warn of rising risk before harm occurs.
probes: Were there leading measures for this hazard?
Did any of them move before the event?
Was there an agreed response when one moved?

subcategories.name: Communication of Measurements
subcategories.definition: How measurement results were presented and shared, and whether they were understood by those who needed them.
probes: Were results shown in a form people could read quickly?
Did results reach the level that could fund a fix?
Were bad results reported as clearly as good ones?

subcategories.name: Continuous Improvement through Measurement
subcategories.definition: Whether measurement was used to drive change and to check that changes worked.
probes: Was a change made because of what measurement showed?
Was the effect of that change measured afterwards?
Were measures updated when the risk picture changed?

subcategories.name: Integration with Technology
subcategories.definition: How instruments, software and data systems supported measurement, and whether they were reliable.
probes: Were the instruments involved calibrated and working?
Did data systems link readings to the right equipment?
Were failures of measuring equipment spotted and fixed?

subcategories.name: Audits and Inspections
subcategories.definition: Planned checks of systems and plant, how they were scoped, and whether their findings were closed.
probes: Did an audit or inspection cover this system before the event?
Was its scope specific to this plant's hazards?
Were its findings closed on time and checked?

chapters.title: Management/Money
chapters.definition: How leadership, management practice and money shaped the resources and decisions behind the work.

subcategories.name: Strategic Financial Planning
subcategories.definition: How long-term budgets were set, and whether they provided for safety-critical needs over the asset's life.
probes: Did long-term budgets include the safety-critical work involved?
Were known future needs funded before they became urgent?
Did plans allow for ageing equipment and rising risk?

subcategories.name: Leadership and Decision-Making
subcategories.definition: How managers made decisions that affected risk, and whether they used the information available to them.
probes: Did managers have the facts they needed for the key decision?
Was the decision made at the right level?
Were warnings from staff weighed in the decision?

subcategories.name: Budgeting and Resource Allocation
subcategories.definition: How yearly money and staff were divided up, and whether safety-related items were cut or deferred.
probes: Was safety-related work deferred because of budget?
Were requests for funds for this system turned down?
Did the budget process show the risk of deferring?

subcategories.name: Training and Development Investments
subcategories.definition: How much the organisation invested in people's skills, and whether it matched the risks they managed.
probes: Was training for this task funded and scheduled?
Were training cuts made in the period before the event?
Did investment in skills match the hazards people faced?

subcategories.name: Risk Management and Compliance
subcategories.definition: How management identified, assessed and controlled risks, and met legal and company requirements.
probes: Was this risk on a register with an owner?
Were the controls assessed as adequate by someone competent?
Did known legal requirements for this system get met?

subcategories.name: Investment in Infrastructure and Technology
subcategories.definition: Spending on plant, equipment and systems, and whether known upgrades were made in time.
probes: Was a needed upgrade known before the event?
Was it approved, and if so, was it carried out?
Did deferral of the upgrade have a recorded risk review?

subcategories.name: Performance Monitoring and Accountability
subcategories.definition: How management tracked whether agreed work was done, and followed up when it was not.
probes: Were overdue actions on this system tracked by management?
Did anyone follow up when actions slipped?
Were extensions to deadlines approved by the right person?

subcategories.name: Stakeholder Engagement and Communication
subcategories.definition: How management talked with staff, contractors, owners and regulators about risk and performance.
probes: Were contractors and staff told about the risks of this job?
Did management report the true state of the risk upward?
Were concerns from outside parties answered?

subcategories.name: Financial Controls and Auditing
subcategories.definition: How spending decisions were checked, and whether controls on cost had side effects on safety.
probes: Did a cost control affect a safety-related purchase?
Were purchase approvals timely for urgent safety items?
Did financial reviews look at safety consequences?

subcategories.name: Continuous Improvement and Adaptability
subcategories.definition: Whether management learned from events and changed resources and practices as conditions changed.
probes: Did management act on lessons from earlier events?
Were resources shifted when a new risk appeared?
Was there a review of management practice after near misses?

chapters.title: Machine
chapters.definition: The equipment, tools, instruments and technology used in the work, from design through to retirement.

subcategories.name: Design and Suitability
subcategories.definition: Whether the equipment was designed and chosen for the duty, pressure, material and conditions it actually met.
probes: Was the equipment rated for the duty it was used for?
Did its design allow for the failure that happened?
Were known design weaknesses reviewed and dealt with?

subcategories.name: Maintenance and Reliability
subcategories.definition: How reliable the equipment was in service, and whether its condition supported safe operation.
probes: Was the equipment working as intended at the time?
Had it failed in the same way before?
Was its reliability tracked by anyone?

subcategories.name: Integration and Compatibility
subcategories.definition: Whether parts, systems and connections worked together as intended, including after changes.
probes: Were the parts fitted compatible with the original design?
Did a change to one part affect how another worked?
Was compatibility checked when parts were substituted?

subcategories.name: Automation and Control Systems
subcategories.definition: How control, shutdown and safety systems were set up, and whether they acted without waiting for people.
probes: Did an automatic shutdown or interlock exist for this case?
Did the control system act in the time needed?
Were bypassed or manual-only functions known and managed?

subcategories.name: Ergonomics and Usability
subcategories.definition: Whether controls, displays and tools were easy to use correctly and hard to use wrongly.
probes: Were controls and displays easy to read and operate?
Could a control be operated in the wrong way easily?
Were users involved in choosing the equipment?

subcategories.name: Monitoring and Diagnostics
subcategories.definition: How equipment reported its own condition, through detectors, gauges and alarms, and whether that was seen.
probes: Were detectors and gauges in place where they were needed?
Did they give a warning early enough to act?
Were faulty or bypassed detectors known and tracked?

subcategories.name: Safety Features and Risk Mitigation
subcategories.definition: The engineered protections on the equipment, such as relief, isolation and containment, and their condition.
probes: Were the engineered protections on this equipment in place?
Did they work when called on?
Was the protection level matched to the hazard?

subcategories.name: Lifecycle Management
subcategories.definition: How equipment was managed from purchase to retirement, including ageing, obsolescence and timely replacement.
probes: Was the equipment past its planned replacement point?
Were ageing items identified and scheduled for renewal?
Did replacement decisions consider the risk of waiting?

subcategories.name: Environmental Impact and Sustainability
subcategories.definition: How the equipment's releases, emissions and failures could affect people and surroundings outside the work area.
probes: Could a failure of this equipment harm the surroundings?
Were release paths and their effects understood?
Did design choices limit the size of a possible release?

subcategories.name: Training and Competence
subcategories.definition: Whether people knew the equipment well enough to operate, check and recover it safely.
probes: Were operators familiar with this particular equipment?
Did they know its failure modes and warning signs?
Were vendor instructions available and understood?

chapters.title: Material
chapters.definition: The materials, parts, consumables and substances used or handled, including their quality, supply and handling.

subcategories.name: Material Quality
subcategories.definition: Whether materials and parts met their specification and were fit for the service they went into.
probes: Did the parts used meet the specified grade and type?
Was the quality of incoming material checked?
Had poor-quality material caused trouble before?

subcategories.name: Material Availability and Supply Chain
subcategories.definition: Whether the right materials were in stock or obtainable in time, and how supply gaps were handled.
probes: Were the right parts available when the job needed them?
Did a supply delay lead to a substitute being used?
Were long lead-time items ordered ahead of need?

subcategories.name: Material Compatibility
subcategories.definition: Whether materials suited each other, the process fluid and the conditions, including any substitutes.
probes: Was the material compatible with the process fluid and pressure?
Was a substitute part assessed before use?
Did a change of material go through a change review?

subcategories.name: Storage and Handling
subcategories.definition: How materials and substances were stored, moved and handled so that they stayed safe and in good condition.
probes: Were materials stored in a way that kept them in good condition?
Was the handling of hazardous substances controlled?
Were stored items labelled so the right one was picked?

subcategories.name: Material Waste and Sustainability
subcategories.definition: How waste, spills and spent materials were managed, and whether they added hazards.
probes: Did waste or spent material add a hazard at the scene?
Were spills and leftovers cleared under a set routine?
Was disposal of hazardous material controlled?

subcategories.name: Material Cost Management
subcategories.definition: How the cost of materials influenced choices, and whether cheaper options were checked for risk.
probes: Was a cheaper part chosen over the specified one?
Was the risk of the cheaper option assessed?
Did cost rules slow down buying the right part?

subcategories.name: Compliance and Regulatory Requirements
subcategories.definition: Whether materials and their handling met the legal and company rules that applied to them.
probes: Did the materials meet the rules that applied to them?
Were certificates for critical materials on file?
Were legal handling requirements for substances met?

subcategories.name: Material Traceability
subcategories.definition: Whether the source, batch and history of a part could be traced from purchase to installation.
probes: Could the part fitted be traced to its source and batch?
Were locally bought parts recorded like stock items?
Did records show which part went into which equipment?

subcategories.name: Innovation and Material Advancements
subcategories.definition: Whether better materials or designs were known and considered, especially for repeat failures.
probes: Was a better material known for this repeat failure?
Was it considered and, if not used, why not?
Did suppliers or specialists offer advice on the material?

subcategories.name: Emergency and Contingency Planning
subcategories.definition: Whether materials needed in an emergency, such as foam, spares or sealing kits, were ready and sufficient.
probes: Were emergency materials stocked and ready?
Was there enough of them for an event of this size?
Were they checked on a set schedule?

chapters.title: Maintenance
chapters.definition: How equipment was kept working and reliable through inspection, servicing, repair and testing over its whole life.

subcategories.name: Preventive Maintenance Programme
subcategories.definition: The planned, routine servicing meant to stop equipment failing, and whether it covered what mattered.
probes: Was this equipment in a planned maintenance routine?
Was the routine done on time before the event?
Did the routine cover the part that failed?

subcategories.name: Predictive Maintenance and Condition Monitoring
subcategories.definition: How the condition of equipment was measured over time to catch wear, corrosion or damage early.
probes: Was the condition of this equipment measured over time?
Did measurements show wear or thinning before the event?
Were those results acted on within a set time?

subcategories.name: Corrective Maintenance Execution
subcategories.definition: How faults and defects were repaired, and whether repairs were done properly and checked after.
probes: Were known defects on this equipment repaired?
Was the repair done to the correct standard?
Was the repaired item tested before it went back into service?

subcategories.name: Maintenance Planning and Scheduling
subcategories.definition: How maintenance work was planned, prioritised and fitted around operations.
probes: Was the maintenance job planned with the right steps and parts?
Was it given priority in line with its risk?
Did operations pressure move or shorten the job?

subcategories.name: Maintenance Personnel Competence
subcategories.definition: Whether the people doing maintenance had the skills, authority and guidance for the specific job.
probes: Were the maintainers trained on this equipment?
Did they have the vendor guidance for the job?
Was the work checked by someone qualified?

subcategories.name: Maintenance Documentation and Records
subcategories.definition: Whether maintenance history, work orders and test results were recorded and could be used to spot patterns.
probes: Was the maintenance history for this item complete?
Did the records show repeat work on the same fault?
Were test results recorded and kept?

subcategories.name: Spare Parts and Inventory Management
subcategories.definition: Whether the right spares were stocked, identified and issued for maintenance work.
probes: Were the correct spares in stock for this equipment?
Was the spare issued checked against the specification?
Were critical spares identified and kept at a minimum level?

subcategories.name: Maintenance Technology and Tools
subcategories.definition: The tools, test equipment and systems used to plan and carry out maintenance, and whether they were adequate.
probes: Did maintainers have the right tools and test rigs?
Was the work management system used to plan the job?
Were special tools for this equipment available?

subcategories.name: Software and Control System Maintenance
subcategories.definition: How control logic, detectors, alarms and safety systems were tested, updated and kept working.
probes: Were safety systems and detectors proof-tested on schedule?
Were changes to control logic recorded and reviewed?
Were faults in alarms or detectors fixed quickly?

subcategories.name: Safety in Maintenance Activities
subcategories.definition: How hazards during maintenance itself were controlled, through permits, isolation and return-to-service checks.
probes: Was the maintenance job under a valid permit?
Were isolations made and proven before the work?
Was there a formal check before return to service?

subcategories.name: Continuous Improvement in Maintenance
subcategories.definition: How maintenance learned from repeat failures and changed its routines, intervals and methods.
probes: Did repeat failures trigger a root-cause review?
Were maintenance intervals changed after earlier findings?
Was the outcome of changes checked later?
